gallery.title: File:HabsburgStammtafelGruftFerdinand27.png
gallery.credit: Own work Compiled by Stan Zegel, 2005
gallery.description:
Family of Emperor Ferdinand III who are buried in the Kaisergruft in Vienna, showing relationships, life spans, and tomb numbers, as described in w:Imperial Crypt.
This graph also illustrates the seeds of the w:War of the Austrian Succession after the extinction of the male line with the death of Emperor Karl VI (40). Although the late emperor wanted his daughter Maria Theresia (56) to succeed him despite the w:salic law barring women from the crown, she was the daughter of merely the younger brother and the husband of the older brother's (35) daughter took to arms, successfully, because his wife had seniority to the claim.
It also illustrates how Empress Maria Theresia and her sister(39) married two brothers descended from her great aunt (18).

The number before a person's name corresponds with that person's entry in the detailed listing of occupants of each Vault, to which it is hyperlinked. When necessary to establish continuity, a person buried elsewhere is assigned a number preceded by an x and then listed in the Selected Other Habsburgs section.

gallery.title: File:HabsburgStammtafelGruftFounders.png
gallery.description:
Family of the founders of the Kaisergruft in Vienna, showing those buried there, their relationships, life spans, and tomb numbers as described in w:Imperial Crypt.
Note that the beginning of the chart shows the great dynastic marriages that brought the Habsburg dynasty its widespread territories: Maximilian I to the heiress of Burgundy (bringing the Netherlands), their son Philip to the heiress of Spain, their son Ferdinand to Anne of Bohemia (bringing the crowns of Bohemia and Hungary).

The number before a person's name corresponds with that person's entry in the detailed listing of occupants of each Vault, to which it is hyperlinked. When necessary to establish continuity, a person buried elsewhere is assigned a number preceded by an x and then listed in the Selected Other Habsburgs section.

gallery.description:
Descendants of Emperor Franz II who are buried in the Imperial Crypt in Vienna, showing relationships, life spans and tomb numbers as described in w:Imperial Crypt. Compiled by Stan Zegel, 2005.
The number before a person's name corresponds with that person's entry in the detailed listing of occupants of each Vault, to which it is hyperlinked. Compiler's Note: Number 79 is really the daughter of Grand Duke Ferdinand III of Tuscany, so should be shown instead on Image:HabsburgStammtafelGruftTuscan.png and not here. I will correct this later, because the master copy of this Zegelchart has been corrupted and must be reconstructed before I can amend this graphic.

gallery.title: File:HabsburgStammtafelGruftMTheresia56.png
gallery.credit: Own work; Compiled by Stan Zegel, 2005.
gallery.description:
Descendants of Empress Maria Theresia buried in the Kaisergruft in Vienna, showing relationships, life spans and tomb numbers as described in w:Imperial Crypt.
The male line of the Habsburgs having died out with Maria Theresia's father Karl VI, through her marriage to Franz Stephen of Lorraine (Lothringen) the family became the House of Habsburg-Lorraine.
Note the role of Maria Karoline's(107) daughters in establishing the surviving senior lines of the dynasty by marrying their first cousins, the sons of her brother Leopold II(113).

The number before a person's name corresponds with that person's entry in the detailed listing of occupants of each Vault, to which it is hyperlinked. When necessary to establish continuity, a person buried elsewhere is assigned a number preceded by an x and then listed in the Selected Other Habsburgs section.
